claims.text: The melting properties of refractory materials can be accurately calculated using an ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT combined with machine-learning interpolation.
Machine-learning interpolation reduces the computational cost of ab initio free-energy calculations.
The material is solid at standard temperature and pressure.
Electronic structure and atomic arrangement mediate the calculation of melting properties.
Quantum-mechanical calculations provide free energy as a function of temperature and pressure.
The calculated free-energy dependence on temperature and pressure can be used to determine melting properties.
The predicted melting temperature will be within 10% of the experimental value.
The predicted entropy of fusion will be within 5% of the experimental value.
The predicted enthalpy of fusion will be within 5% of the experimental value.
The predicted volume change at the melting point will be within 2% of the experimental value.
The proposed method applies to refractory materials with melting temperatures above 2000 K.
Machine-learning model accuracy affects the reliability of the calculated melting properties.
The choice of DFT exchange-correlation functional affects the reliability of the calculated melting properties.
Convergence of thermodynamic integration affects the reliability of the calculated melting properties.
